summary: Attacked the extraction of Koymans–Pagano, 'On Stevenhagen's conjecture' (arXiv 2201.13424v1, still the only version; accepted by Acta Mathematica but not yet published: Crossref has no record). It has 264 items, 6 routes and 51 source issues. The mathematics of the extraction holds. Every numbered statement has an item. Theorem 1.1 and α ≈ 0.4194224 recompute, and the Markov-chain limit gives 1 − α. E1–E51 hold. The seven cited library declarations give their items. There are thirteen findings: five medium, eight low, none high. (1) Five items marked planned are built in Tau Ceti f790474. They are the continuous cochain complex Z¹/d¹ (/36, /52), corestriction with an arbitrary transversal, which is (3.1)–(3.2) (/83), the maximal pro-p quotient (/28), and the Kummer map giving χ_γ (/21). (2) Genus theory (/227) is built: the ramified primes generate Cl⁺[2] and the genus characters span the dual of Cl⁺/Cl⁺². So is /5's 'kernel of Cl⁺ → Cl has order ≤ 2'. (3) The bilinear Legendre-symbol estimate is Smith's Prop. 6.6 from Jutila (1975), not Heath-Brown's quadratic large sieve. The paper never cites Heath-Brown's large sieve, yet route 5, the brief and the prerequisites ask SV.2 for the wrong and much harder theorem. (4) P(m, n, j) (/211) goes to the Part II, while the accepted ST blueprint owns it at ST.5 (as the extraction itself does for P_Sym and (A.2)). (5) Route 2 sends the 𝒪_K/ℤ[√d] unit passage for /5, /9, /12 to CA.4. The CA blueprint owns it at CA.5 and only for d ≢ 1 mod 4, which excludes every odd d ∈ 𝒟. Low: (6) the review's strike of E12's 'at most 2' is wrong (counterexample S = {65}, ψ = 0, p = 5), and E12 now contradicts itself and /104; (7) /69's note gets the rank formula wrong (A = ℤ/4); (8) §4 allows a = 1, which makes Theorem 4.6(b)'s support dependent; (9) Lemma 6.3 cites Smith 'Lemma 4.1' (it is Prop. 4.1 in v2) and omits r ≥ 2, and /159's note is out of date; (10) the p. 3 effectivity claim rests on CKMP's m = 2 case, which uses Siegel's theorem; (11) the prerequisites omit Rédei, Rédei–Reichardt, Heilbronn, MacWilliams, Watkins and Jutila; (12) three '(issues file)' references have no entry; (13) sourceVersions is missing although E4 and E7 quote stated results.

The extraction PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO is by cc-39fac3 (issue #2194, commit 20bd7afe), and its review REV-PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO is by cc-d67081 (issue #2195, commit 8d835d12). cc-f805bf appears in none of the four target files (.result.json, .md, .review.json, reviews/REV-PAPER-KOYMANS-PAGANO.md). Disclosure. This session wrote FIX-RT-AUDIT-07, the fix of the library audit covering ArithmeticStatistics and SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns (including ST.0, ST.4 and the SV.2 duality target), and FIX-RT-AREA-finitefields. Findings 3 (SV.2 as owner of the large-sieve input) and 4 (ST.5 as owner of P(m, n, j)) touch layers that audit covers. Neither finding relies on any audit value that FIX-RT-AUDIT-07 changed: finding 3 rests on the paper, Smith and Crossref, and finding 4 on the ArithmeticStatistics packet. FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums is not touched.

The source, 29 September 2026. The arXiv abstract page for 2201.13424 lists only v1 (31 January 2022, no journal reference). https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.13424v1 and the unversioned PDF both have SHA-256 c7a93ffea06491d824d900fe067f6768246e84555fa8da8282833caac7850cbd, the hash the extraction records. Koymans's publication page still says 'arXiv, To Appear in Acta Mathematica'. Crossref's Acta Mathematica listing (ISSN 0001-5962) runs through vol. 236 no. 2 (2026) without the paper, and a bibliographic Crossref query finds no record. So no published version exists to compare.

The whole paper, pp. 1–110, read in the text layer (pdftotext), in three parts: §§1–4 (pp. 1–34), §§5–6 (pp. 35–59), and §§7–8 with the bibliography (pp. 59–110). Page images at 300 dpi for pp. 39, 44, 53, 54, 59, 74, 75 and 78, and at 150 dpi for pp. 71 and 73. The TeX source (SHA-256 d6c9d917…, as recorded) was used for typography.

Coverage: every numbered statement has an item with a correct locator. That is Propositions 2.1–2.3, 2.5, 2.6, 2.9, 2.14–2.16; Definitions 2.4, 2.8, 2.12; Remarks 2.7, 2.10, 2.17; Corollary 2.11; Lemmas 2.13, 2.18; §2.3; §3.1 and Definition 3.1; Theorem 3.2; Proposition 3.3; Corollary 3.4; Lemma 3.5; Proposition 3.6; Remarks 4.1, 4.3; Definition 4.2; Proposition 4.4; Lemma 4.5; Theorem 4.6; Definitions 5.1, 5.4, 5.8, 5.9; Theorems 5.2, 5.3, 5.5–5.7, 5.10, 5.11; Definition 6.1; Proposition 6.2; Lemma 6.3; Remark 6.4; Lemma 6.5; Proposition 6.6; Lemmas 6.7–6.10; Definitions 7.1, 7.3–7.5, 7.9; Theorems 7.2, 7.10, 7.13; Propositions 7.6, 7.8, 7.12; Lemma 7.7; Remark 7.11; Definitions 8.3, 8.4, 8.6, 8.9, 8.11; Theorems 8.1, 8.2, 8.7, 8.8, 8.10, 8.13; Lemmas 8.5, 8.12. Unnumbered inputs also have items: Hasse–Minkowski, Dirichlet, [FK1, Lemma 1], Smith's (1.2), Hilbert reciprocity, H²(Ẑ, 𝔽₂) = 0, the ℚ₂ self-cup subspace, the ℤ/4 transfer, Erdős–Kac on 𝒟, Sathe–Selberg, the quadratic-character PNT, Landau's repulsion, the effective exceptional-zero bound, Heilbronn, Hoeffding, Chebyshev, MacWilliams, Rédei's 4-rank formula and genus theory. Massey and spin symbols appear only as motivation (the proof of Theorem 5.5 uses cup products and Hilbert reciprocity), so no FIMR spin item is needed. No Siegel–Walfisz theorem is used.

Item statements checked against the text: all of /1–/264. The hypotheses added in /41, /46, /48, /56, /57, /67 are right. Also checked: x versus x₀ in Theorems 5.6 and 5.7 (on the p. 44 image); b | 2d₀ in Theorem 5.10(i); the constants of Proposition 6.2 against Smith Prop. 3.2; Lemma 6.3's constants (p. 53 image); /173 (C₀, the range of i); /198 (s_i < (2/3)s_{i+1}, 100 ≤ C_compr ≤ (log N)^{100}); /208 (the constant tuple of the proof of Theorem 7.13); /213 (Theorem 8.1 with m ≥ 2, n₂…n_{m+1}, and error A|𝒟(N)|/(log log log log N)^{c/(m²6^m)}); /221 and /223 (k_gap, n_max); /219 (m ≥ 3).

Main theorem and constants, recomputed. α = ∏_{j odd}(1 − 2^{−j}) = 0.4194224418, so 1 − α = 0.5805775582. The identity [KP3, (A.2)] holds exactly for m = 0, …, 7. P(n, n, j)/2^n matches CKMP's Q(n₂|n₃) and the Markov-chain reading of Theorem 8.1. The limiting symmetric-matrix law, weighted by P₂(m) = 1/(2^{m+1} − 1), sums to 0.58057756 = 1 − α. The constants of Theorem 7.13 satisfy Proposition 7.8's constraints. In /264, ε < 1/a and log M_box ≥ A_Comb·6^{m+1}·log ε⁻¹. The Hoeffding step of (8.12) (/231) gives exp(−4k_gap/(log log log N)²), within the stated O.

Derivations redone: (2.3) from the semidirect-product law; the centre of 𝔽₂≀𝔽₂^m; the Art_s kernel reduction (/69; see finding 7); Remark 4.1; Proposition 2.16 place by place; Proposition 3.3 via the transfer; Proposition 3.6(b) when χ_i∘i₂* = χ₅; the steps (4.4)–(4.9) of the proof of Theorem 4.6 and its Rédei admissibility check; the whole place-by-place proof of Theorem 5.5; Theorem 5.2's total-reality checks; Lemma 6.7's commutator identity; Lemma 6.8(b); Lemma 6.10's pointer relation for |S| = 3; Proposition 6.6 from Smith's Proposition 4.4 (finding 9(c)); Smith's Proposition 6.6 from Jutila (finding 3).

Source issues E1–E51, each at its locator. All hold as recorded, except that the review's amendment to E12 is wrong (finding 6). Independently re-verified: E4's s = 1 counterexample (½ against 0); E7 (a = 5 gives ℚ(ζ₅), ramified at ∞); E9; E12's second half; E13's Hilbert-symbol repair; E15; E16–E28, including E17 (both sums over q | a₁ vanish by Hilbert reciprocity for (χ, a₁)) and E18 (replacing ψ_{s+1}(x₀) by ψ_{s+1}(x₀) + χ_{x₀} flips φ_{[s]} at σ_p); E29–E51, including E41 (Theorem 8.2 needs m ≥ 3), E46 (only δ ≤ exp(−e^{(0.3−o(1))k_gap}) follows), E48 (the Cauchy–Schwarz repair works) and E51 (Crossref gives Gerth's pages as 489–515). The review's changes. E12 is wrong (finding 6). E13's added symptom (the empty base set when s = 1) is right. E17 and E18, as restricted, are right. Checked against the page images, as the review did: the review's E30 remark on ℳ versus M in Definition 7.4 (p. 60) is right.

findings.claim: Five items are marked planned, citing ProfiniteCohomology Layers 2, 6 and 9 and ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 3 only as plans. What they need is built in Tau Ceti at f790474. (a) /36: continuous 1-cocycles in an ambient group of continuous 1-cochains, with the inhomogeneous differential (d¹f)(g,h) = g·f(h) − f(gh) + f(g). This is exactly d_x for the module N(χ_x), since g acts on N(χ_x) by (−1)^{χ_x(g)}. (b) /52: the paper's d on 𝔽₂-valued cochains. It is applied only to 1-cochains in the paper (to get (2.3) on p. 15 and in the proof of Lemma 6.7 on p. 56), and there it is d¹ for the trivial action. (c) /83: corestriction on H¹ for an open subgroup of finite index, computed with any transversal. With trivial 𝔽₂ coefficients and the transversal {1, σ} of an index-2 subgroup, the library formula (cor¹_t f)(γ) = Σ_u f(ℓ_u(γ)), where ℓ_u(γ) = t(u)⁻¹·γ·t(γ⁻¹u), gives cor(χ)(σ) = χ(σ²) and cor(χ)(τ) = χ(τ) + χ(σ⁻¹τσ). These are (3.1) and (3.2), since χ(σ⁻¹τσ) = χ(στσ⁻¹) for a character of the index-2 subgroup. H¹ with trivial action is identified with continuous homomorphisms. (d) /28: the maximal pro-p quotient G ⧸ proPKernel p G, with its universal property, is built. At p = 2 and G = G_ℚ it is the paper's 𝒢_ℚ^{pro-2}; the item's own note says so. (e) /21: the Kummer map K^× → H¹(G_K, μ_n), with the explicit cocycle g ↦ gα/α, is built. At n = 2 the action on μ₂ is trivial, and H1EquivOfSmulEqSelf turns the class of γ into the continuous character χ_γ. The Kummer isomorphism, which is not built, is not needed to define χ_γ. The reviewed library audit (data/library-coverage.json) records all of this: PC Layer 2 'partly built' with C1, C2, Z1, Z2, B1, B2, H0, H1, H2 present; PC Layer 6 'Corestriction in degrees 0, 1, 2 for a variable transversal … tauceti'; PC Layer 9 connecting map δ⁰ 'tauceti'; ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 3 'proPKernel and the maximal pro-p quotient … tauceti'. Protocol §16 makes an item library when Mathlib or Tau Ceti has it at the pinned commits. Left as it is, the Part II design would plan objects that already exist.

findings.claim: Item 227 has two genus-theory surjections: 𝔽₂^r → Cl(ℚ(√x))[2], e ↦ [Up(∏p_i^{e_i})], and 𝔽₂^r → Cl^∨(ℚ(√x))[2], e ↦ Σe_iχ_{p_i}, with Cl the narrow class group. The item marks both as planned in Multiquadratic Layers 2–3, but the reviewed audit rates those layers 'built' and Tau Ceti f790474 proves both. (i) The 2-torsion of the narrow class group of any quadratic field is generated by the narrow classes of the ramified primes, with no signature hypothesis. That is the first surjection, because Up(∏p_i^{e_i}) is the product of the ramified primes above the p_i. (ii) For a prime-discriminant factorization of the discriminant, the family of singleton genus characters is injective on Cl⁺/Cl⁺², and its docstring adds 'Equivalently, the #s genus characters span the full dual of Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²'. That is the second surjection. For x ∈ 𝒟 the prime discriminants are p_i (p_i ≡ 1 mod 4) and 8 when 2 | x, and χ₈ = χ₂. Item 5's note also calls 'the kernel of Cl⁺ → Cl has order at most 2' a missing step, but that is library too.

findings.claim: The extraction names the wrong theorem as the analytic input of (7.11) and (8.46), and routes it to SV.2 under that name. Item 189's note says 'For t₁ < t_i < t₁^{3/2} one needs Heath-Brown's large sieve for quadratic characters'. Route 5, the brief and the prerequisites attribute the bilinear Legendre-symbol estimate to Heath-Brown (Acta Arith. 1995). The paper never cites that work. Its only Heath-Brown reference, [22], is the Selmer-groups paper, which is mentioned only in §1. The paper cites [42, Proposition 6.6] (Smith). Smith proves Prop. 6.6 from Jutila's 1975 mean-value lemma. Jutila's bound gives the estimate in the whole range t₁ < t_i, with no case distinction: Σ_{x₁}(Σ_{x₂} c(x₂)(x₁/x₂))² ≪ t₁|X₂| + t₁^{1/2}t₂² log⁶t₂, and Cauchy–Schwarz then gives Σ_{x₁}|Σ_{x₂}| ≪ t₁t₂^{1/2} + t₁^{3/4}t₂ log³t₂ ≪ t₂t₁^{3/4+ε}. Here t₁t₂^{1/2} ≤ t₁^{3/4}t₂ because t₁ ≤ t₂. Heath-Brown's theorem is much deeper and is not what the source uses. The note's remark about the classical multiplicative large sieve is correct: it gives (t₁² + t₂)|X₂| for the second moment and hence the bound only when t₂ ≥ t₁^{3/2}. findings.claim: Route 2 sends the negative-Pell reformulations to CA.4 ('Classical Diophantine equations') alone. These are items 5 and 12 (narrow class group criteria) and item 9 (the Galois-module structure of the unit group). Their common missing step is the passage between integral solutions of x² − dy² = −1, i.e. units of ℤ[√d] of norm −1, and units of 𝒪_K of norm −1. The Tau Ceti side, 'Cl⁺ → Cl injective iff some unit of 𝒪_K has norm −1', is already built. The CA blueprint places that passage in CA.5 ('Number-field arithmetic handoff … unit and class groups'), not CA.4. Its node is restricted to d ≢ 1 (mod 4). Every odd d ∈ 𝒟 is ≡ 1 (mod 4), being a product of primes ≡ 1 (mod 4). So the planned node covers only the even members of 𝒟. It misses exactly the case the extraction's note on item 5 flags: for d ≡ 5 (mod 8), a unit (a + b√d)/2 with a, b odd has cube in ℤ[√d]. For d ≡ 1 (mod 8), 𝒪_K^× ⊆ ℤ[√d], since a² − db² ≡ a² − b² ≡ 0 (mod 8) for odd a, b rules out norm ±4. As routed, the owner that CA.4 imports would not supply what items 5 and 12 need for most of 𝒟.

findings.claim: The review struck the first half of E12, and that change is wrong. E12 now contradicts itself. Its correction ends 'The ramification index in the first sentence does equal 2, so nothing is wrong there', but its reason still says ''Equals 2' fails for trivial raw cocycles (L(0) = ℚ); only e ≤ 2 is ever used'. Item 104 still says ''equals 2' should be 'is at most 2''. The review's justification, 'K ⊆ ∏_x L(ψ_{k+1}(x)) forces e_p ≥ 2', assumes something Lemma 4.5 does not: a raw cocycle may be 0, and then L(0) = ℚ. Counterexample: S = {65}, k = 1, ψ₂(65) = 0. This is a raw cocycle for N(65) (Definition 2.8: an element of Cocy_unr(G_ℚ, N(χ))[4]). 65 ≡ 1 (mod 8), so (2) splits in K = ℚ(√65) and its decomposition group is trivial, hence cyclic. The prime 5 ramifies in K, but ∏L = ℚ, so the ramification index of 5 is 1, not 2. The index is always ≤ 2: the compositum with K is unramified over K at finite places, inertia at odd p is tame of exponent 2, and at (2) the lemma's hypothesis applies. The index equals 2 when each L(ψ_{k+1}(x)) contains ℚ(√x), as in every application, where 2^kψ_{k+1}(x) restricts nontrivially.

findings.claim: The note says 'Hence rk_{2^s} A = dim of 2^{s−1}A[2^s] minus the dimension of the left kernel'. That is false. With rk_{2^s} A = dim 2^{s−1}A[2^s] (item 211's convention), the left kernel 2^s·A[2^{s+1}] has dimension rk_{2^{s+1} A. The correct consequences are: rank of Art_s = rk_{2^s} A − rk_{2^{s+1} A, and rk_{2^{s+1} A = dim(left kernel). Counterexample: A = ℤ/4, s = 1. Then A[2] = {0, 2} has dimension 1 and the left kernel 2·A[4] = {0, 2} has dimension 1, so the note gives rk₂ A = 0, while rk₂(ℤ/4) = 1. §8 uses the correct form: the 2^{m+1}-rank is the dimension of the kernel of Art_m. A Part II worker taking the note as the API statement would get the Markov chain's step wrong.

findings.claim: The §4 set-up allows a = 1, and then Theorem 4.6(b) is ill-formed. The set-up says only 'Let a be a divisor of d₀'. Remark 4.1 derives a > 0 but not a ≠ 1. With a = 1 and ψ_{s+1}(x) = 0 for all x ∈ C − {x₀}, (4.1) holds (2^s·0 = 0 = χ₁). The first two conditions of Definition 4.2 hold trivially, and conditions 3–5 involve only the p_i(h) and d₀. So the triple can be profitable. Theorem 4.6(b) then asserts an expansion map 'with support {χ_{p_i(1)p_i(2)} : i ∈ [s]} ∪ {χ_a} and pointer χ_a', where χ_a = 0. Definition 2.12 requires a linearly independent support. The proof's appeal to Theorem 3.2 also needs Ram(ℚ(χ_a)/ℚ) ≠ ∅ (§3.1). Every use in §§5 and 8.4 has a > 1: in §8.4, a comes from a nonzero kernel vector. So nothing downstream breaks, but items 98, 107 and 108 inherit the missing hypothesis.

findings.claim: Two recorded mistakes, E4 and E7, have affects 'a stated result', but the file has no sourceVersions. Protocol §18 requires it as soon as a finding quotes a stated result, and scripts/check_errata.py enforces that rule on errata files. The reading is described only in prose in source.readSections.
